title: Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: Tax, Super, and Salary Sacrifice HECS Debt Explained
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, Medicare, and how salary sacrifice HECS debt affects take-home pay.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, before tax, super, and any salary sacrifice HECS debt adjustments.

faqs.q: Does the annual estimate include casual loading?
faqs.a: No, the base calculation uses your ordinary hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, you may receive a 25% loading on top. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. The calculator has a checkbox to add 25% loading, but you should never type a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on the annual figure?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. It stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage, that is about $52,270 gross, so super would be an extra $6,272 per year.

faqs.q: What tax brackets apply to my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2%. These are applied to your taxable income, which may be reduced by salary sacrifice arrangements such as HECS debt repayments.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you earn an hourly wage or have received a salary offer, converting between the two is straightforward. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees, the benchmark is 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work a different pattern, simply substitute your usual weekly hours.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The 38-hour week is the standard ordinary hours for full-time employment under many awards and the National Employment Standards. Multiplying by 52 weeks gives a full-year figure. If you are part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours to your actual average.

For example, on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour:
- Weekly pay: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (rounded to $1,004.9 per the Fair Work Ombudsman)
- Fortnightly pay: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44
- Annual gross: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44

### Casual Loading and Award Rates

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is therefore $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using the [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add casual loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

Award rates vary by industry and classification. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides that list minimum hourly rates for each award. These rates may be higher than the National Minimum Wage. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Super guarantee contributions are 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer in addition to your salary. For the annual figure above ($52,269.44), super would be an extra $6,272.33 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your total employment cost is higher than your gross pay.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026–27:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a single person earning $52,269, the tax would be approximately $5,167 plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving about $46,057 after tax. This is an estimate; your actual tax depends on deductions, offsets, and other factors.

### Salary Sacrifice HECS Debt and Take-Home Pay

If you have a Higher Education Loan Program (HELP) debt, your employer may deduct repayments through the tax system once your income exceeds the threshold ($51,550 for 2026–27). However, you can also use **salary sacrifice HECS debt** arrangements to reduce your taxable income by sacrificing part of your pre-tax salary into your superannuation. This lowers your assessable income, which can reduce both your income tax and your HELP repayment amount. It is important to understand how salary sacrifice interacts with your HECS debt, as it may affect your overall take-home pay.

For more details on salary packaging and super, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging). You can also check [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimates after tax and Medicare.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the National Minimum Wage example:
- Weekly: $1,004.72
- Fortnightly: $2,009.44
- Annual: $52,269.44

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing salary offers.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Averages

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. Award rates are industry-specific and often higher. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.7 per week (May 2026). This is an average, not a median for any particular job. Do not use it as a substitute for your own rate. For job-specific pay data, refer to [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources.

### Limitations of This Estimate

This conversion assumes a constant hourly rate, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a more personalised calculation, use the [timesheet](/). You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for tax brackets and super caps.
